items.issue: Early exit is per-token, not per-request. A request contains many tokens, each of which may exit at a different depth; the scheduler's unit of work is the token/sequence state, not a request-level exit.

The immediately preceding sentence in the same paragraph defines the unit as token-level: 'Adaptive depth (per-token early exit — the same early-exit interface above) changes the scheduler's unit of work.' The next sentence then attributes exit to requests, contradicting the per-token definition it builds on; L106 also defines the interface as 'a trained head that lets a token leave before the final layer'. items.figure: FIGURE 11.3, panel A (Within one NVLink domain)
items.issue: The printed per-request on-node transfer time (0.08 s) is inconsistent with the figure's own 4-GPU prefill / 4-GPU decode grids and the 'per GPU' rate label. The top line reads '~35 GB ≈ 0.08 s' and the link is labeled '450 GB/s per GPU per direction', but 0.08 s = 35/450 treats the full 35 GB as traversing a single 450 GB/s link. With 4 prefill GPUs and 4 decode GPUs (TP sharding, which is mandatory for the canonical 70B since 140 GB > 80 GB per GPU), the 35 GB KV is split 4 ways and the 4 GPU-pair links run in parallel, so the per-request transfer latency is 35/(4·450) = 8.75/450 ≈ 0.02 s, i.e. 4× smaller than printed. Note 11.3-1 (p.190) repeats the single-link arithmetic: 'at NVLink's 450 GB/s per direction (§9.2) that transfer is 35 ÷ 450 ≈ 0.08 s'.

The bullet asserts an unconditional zeroing; the chapter's own goodput definition makes it continuous: chapter-14.md L51 '| SLO-goodput | tokens/s meeting the SLO (Ch 6), not raw throughput |'. If only the tail of TTFT crosses the deadline, some requests still meet the SLO and goodput is positive but lower; it reaches zero only when no request in the window complies. The claim strength exceeds the mechanism as written.

items.figure: FIGURE 14.1 — Capability screen then deployment benchmark
items.issue: The three orange activity boxes set white text on a mid-luminance orange fill. In grayscale the fill collapses to a mid-gray and the white text loses contrast (roughly 2.4–2.8:1), so the smallest text in the figure — 'Capability MMLU/GSM8K', 'Deploy bench (p95/p99)', 'TCO + SLO gate' — becomes the least legible element on the page, while the dark-navy boxes in the same figure retain high contrast. The figure therefore degrades unevenly in grayscale, and the degradation lands on the labels that carry the figure's actual content.
items.fix_instruction: Set the orange-box labels in near-black (or darken the orange fill) so the text reaches ≥4.5:1 in grayscale, matching the blue row's 5.3:1.
items.evidence: Measured on p250: orange fill RGB(230,126,34), white-on-orange contrast 2.85:1 (matches the finding's 2.4-2.8 range) vs white-on-blue 5.31:1 — the orange boxes carry the figure's content labels ('Capability MMLU/GSM8K', 'Deploy bench (goodput)', 'TCO + SLO gate') at sub-4.5:1 for a print book.
